engine.what: Each emissive meshscatter instance becomes a light that the tracer rebuilds every frame: 7,643 glowing points took 135 s a frame, and 700 took 30 s. Many small glowing things (sparks, fireflies, sound hits) need instanced emitters, or light-sampling that does not rebuild per instance.
Live path tracing still needs over 90 s to give a readable orbit frame and stays visibly grainy.

process: Session 130 had the best idea in a long while, seeing sound with real traced rays, and an honest journal. But the pattern from 127 continues: a new idea, a failed first take posted, and the next idea before the last one is finished. Meanwhile, leftovers from old events (snowballs, tiles, sky islet, balls, sand heap) pile up in the human's island, and the path traced view, the showcase of goal 7, is the worst-looking view right now. Goal 1 (interactions): nothing new to touch; the clap is ambient. Goal 2 (release): nothing released since 24 Nov, and two clap films are broken. Goal 3 (physics): the acoustic ray tracer on Mantle is real progress under the hood. Goal 4/7 (rendering, materials): the traced night clap ring still is the one strong image; everything else is boxes and leftovers. Goal 5 (Lumi): Lumi is bored and lonely (mood 1.0/1.0), and the panel still announces a stale thing. Goal 6 (animation): Lumi's T-pose idle and too-fast wings. Goal 8: the clap is genuinely surprising. Next session: clean the island first (one session, every leftover event undone), then finish the clap as one traced night film that works, released, with a clap key the player can press.

animation.why: live_motion: Lumi's crest and wings swing at 7.4 and 6.9 m/s (too fast to follow), and Cumulus's leg judders 42% from frame to frame. In the strip Lumi holds a stiff T-pose with flapping hands while standing. The clap film has 11 jumps, the largest 0.104 at 0.04 s.

camera.why: The clap film's ear and camera stand inside a tree after the cut (black half), and before it, behind boards and cattails. In the live follow view, with Lumi asleep, the camera looks at an empty path.

creatures.why: The pig, sheep and crab sheets are clean and charming. Wibbles walks through Sir Sniffsalot (clap2.png). A small yellow second Lumi follows the real one in the motion strip (the ghost double, still there). One creature close-up is a frame from inside a green crown.

fun.why: Nothing new to play since 127: the clap fires by itself at night every 45 s with no key and no game. The four mini games are the same four, with the same text in Things to try.

lighting.why: Daylight is still flat and a little murky at noon (14:00 in every shot). The one beautiful light moment is the author's own traced night still of the clap ring (media/s130-seeclap-traced2-boost.png), and it is 480x270 and grainy. In the clap film the sky goes from dark to day in the first second, so the film the human got is a daylight film.

materials.why: In the traced view the grass, sea and trees look rich. The clap film's 'planks' are plain yellow and orange boxes, and the cattails are plastic tubes. The giant snowballs in the traced view are matte white spheres. No glass, metal or subsurface anywhere new this session.

performance.why: Frame median 4.8 ms, p95 8.8 ms, 30 fps. Systems are all under 0.5 ms.

props.why: Generated props are dense and in place (cottage, easels, mushrooms, the wheelbarrow). The new props this session are untextured boxes.

style.why: The soft clay creatures and trees fit together. The leftover snowballs, flat-shaded boxes and smeared sand heap break the look.

ui.why: 'Messages to you' is cut mid-sentence ('The film'). 'New on the island: My day falls over and sings' has been stale since at least session 127. 'Things to try' cuts the jump-in key list in the middle of a line.

world.why: Worse than at 127. The traced view shows two building-sized white spheres and a grey square tile floor in the middle of the island (reviews/p130/traced.png). The raster view has a palm islet floating in the sky, orange and blue balls in mid-air, and a stretched, smeared yellow-orange sand heap that creatures stand on (now.png, orbit2.png). The progress shots for session 130 show the island under snow, and 10 minutes later it is green.

wow.why: The latest post is 'The island answers a clap, a broken take', the sixth failed or broken take in the last ten posts. The second film (see-by-clapping.mp4) is 48 bytes, and ffmpeg cannot read it. A stranger would not share any of these. The idea is shareable; the output is not.

summary: Live in the raster view the island is busy and bright, and the bird Lumi now has a face you notice. The world around it is filling up with leftovers: a palm islet floating in the sky, orange and blue balls hanging in the air, a big smeared sand heap, and in path tracing two huge white snowballs that hide the middle of the island. Seeing sound is the best idea in weeks, but the player gets two failed films (one half black, one a 48-byte file) and a live effect that cannot be seen by day and cannot be played.
